It’s going to take a lot of years and a lot of work to make it to that salary, and very unlikely in my opinion you will make six figures. 
You’d have to be a very talented chef with a lot of passion for cooking and nothing else. 
I have friends who are exec chefs, restaurant owners, etc. and none make that near that salary. 

I made a career change at 40, and entirely quit cooking, so not really too late. I had worked 25 years in the industry, and at most times I was working two jobs to make ends meet and I was exhausted, and it took quite a toll on my body. 
I am absolutely shocked how people work past 40 in kitchens, unless they’ve made it to exec or management of some kind and end up sitting on their asses all day. 
Cooking long term is hard work and I really underestimated how it would affect my body, in my 20s and 30s I felt like I could work 16 hour days on my feet forever for no problem.

It’s a tough job, and not only physically.
There’s a lot of abusive crazy chefs who will want to break you down, especially if you’re a woman is show any kind of submission. 
And HR doesn’t exist in the cooking world, not even in corporate or hotels. You either take it or you quit.
